questions.question: Explain what a line of symmetry is and describe two ways to test whether a line is one. Then explain why a rectangle's diagonal is not a line of symmetry.
questions.expected_answer: A line of symmetry is a line along which a shape can be folded so that the two halves fit exactly on top of each other. Test by folding the cut-out shape, or by standing a mirror on the line and checking that the reflection completes the shape exactly. A rectangle's diagonal makes two equal triangles, but folding along it does not make them land on each other, so it is not a line of symmetry.

questions.question: Draw and count the lines of symmetry of a square, a rectangle that is not a square and an equilateral triangle.
questions.expected_answer: Square: 4 lines, vertical, horizontal and the two diagonals. Rectangle: 2 lines, vertical and horizontal through the centre. Equilateral triangle: 3 lines, each from a corner to the midpoint of the opposite side.

questions.question: Sort the letters A, B, H, S and T by their lines of symmetry and describe each.
questions.expected_answer: A and T each have 1 vertical line. B has 1 horizontal line. H has 2 lines, one vertical and one horizontal. S has no line of symmetry, because no fold makes its halves match.
